title: Collective Coordinate Dynamics of Antiferromagnet: Gravity by Quantum Metric
abstract: The collective coordinate dynamics of antiferromagnetic and ferrimagnetic textures emerges as a geodesic equation governed by the quantum geometry of the CP$^1$ state associated with the Néel vector, rendering an effective Riemannian gravity and a Lorentz force in the texture motion. This unveils a physical scenario fundamentally distinct from the Thiele equation widely used for ferromagnetic textures, which is inertialess without any gravity analogy. Applying our framework to an optically driven ultrafast antiferromagnetic domain wall, we can explain the helicity-dependent asymmetric motion observed experimentally and predict a vibrantly breathing wall width.
summary: This work establishes a novel framework describing the dynamics of magnetic textures in antiferromagnets using a geodesic equation derived from the quantum geometry of the order parameter. By applying this to ultrafast domain wall motion, the authors successfully explain experimentally observed helicity-dependent asymmetries, demonstrating that quantum geometric effects (analogous to gravity) are crucial for accurate modeling.
main_problem: To develop a general collective coordinate dynamics framework for antiferromagnetic (AFM) and ferrimagnetic textures that naturally incorporates gravitational effects arising from the quantum geometry of the associated $	ext{CP}^1$ state.
main_result: The full geodesic dynamics correctly predicts a helicity-dependent asymmetric motion for ultrafast AFM domain walls, which is captured by the geometric connection term, unlike simpler approximations.
method: The authors derive the equation of motion as a geodesic equation governed by a Quantum Geometric Tensor (QGT), which is constructed from the quantum metric and Berry curvature integrated over the system area.
model_or_system: The study focuses on magnetic textures (domain walls) in AFM/ferrimagnets, modeling the dynamics using collective coordinates ($\xi_\mu$) derived from the spin field $\mathbf{n}$ mapping to $	ext{CP}^1$. The resulting dynamics are described by a generalized equation incorporating gravity, friction, and Lorentz forces.
key_observables: Helicity-dependent asymmetric motion of the domain wall center ($X(t)$), and the vibrantly breathing width ($\lambda(t)$).
important_parameters: The AFM limit ($\deltaM 	o 0$), and the comparison between the full geodesic dynamics (G) and the Newtonian approximation (N).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the dynamics can be effectively described by a geodesic equation on the manifold defined by the collective coordinates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup involving an optical pump on an AFM domain wall, showing the time evolution of the domain wall center and width for different pump helicities and theoretical approximations (G vs N).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for a generalized CC framework, derives the geodesic equation using the QGT, and then applies this framework to analyze the ultrafast motion of an AFM domain wall, comparing results against experimental observations.
why_interesting: The emergence of a gravitational term from the quantum geometry of the order parameter provides a novel, geometrically rigorous description for magnetic texture dynamics, which is highly relevant for understanding non-linear dynamics in condensed matter systems.
